data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"A panel of trained non-experts using an explicit checklist will produce more reliable judgments than a single expert's intuition by transforming a high-dimensional pattern-recognition task into a series of low-dimensional binary verifications, reducing the risk of single-point cognitive failure.","counterconditions":[{"case":"The task requires the synthesis of non-linear interactions that cannot be decomposed into a checklist without losing critical information.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"The checklist is under-specified, allowing the panel to rely on collective intuition rather than explicit verification.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"The 'trained' non-experts lack the basic literacy required to interpret the checklist's binary gates correctly.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"The checklist acts as a 'cognitive scaffold' that decomposes the problem into discrete, independent checkpoints. While the expert uses holistic (and thus opaque) pattern matching\u2014which is susceptible to availability bias or fatigue\u2014the panel's process is additive. Reliability gain occurs through the 'Swiss Cheese Model' of error prevention: for a failure to occur, the error must pass through every checklist gate and every panel member's verification of that gate.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
